limitations: The completed journey uses a deterministic mock model and temporary local SQLite through a bounded worker/test drain. It does not claim real-model quality, deployed-worker composition, production-database behavior, or live event-provider integration.
The HTTP POST proves durable asynchronous intake only; it does not execute the model or complete the artifact inline.

The browser gate uses deterministic same-origin discovery and receipt fixtures with the real local session boundary. It proves the control surface and transport contract, not browser-observed worker completion.
The recommended UTC time is a calculated draft field only. The demo does not enroll an attendee, mutate a calendar, create a provider schedule, invoke a messaging connector, or send a reminder.
Event, signup, attendee, and channel values are synthetic or caller-supplied test data and are not independently verified against a live event system.

Determinism covers normalized business payloads. Durable identities, audit records, correlations, and timestamps remain intentionally unique or clock-derived, and DEMO-05 and DEMO-06 remain separately owned.
